interview.purpose: It is for making a personalised birthday storybook with your child as the main character. I can imagine it being useful for parents looking for a quick, meaningful present.
interview.worst_moment: The generated book was the worst moment. I chose crayon style and got pop-art artwork, the title was misspelled, the story was frightening and unrelated in places, and the final sentence stopped halfway through.
interview.best_moment: The best moment was entering Aarav's details, Rory, Abbey Park and the cloud-shape memory. That part felt quick and exciting because I could see a real birthday present taking shape.
interview.abandon: I would probably have abandoned it at the preview. Reading nine pages only to find the important memory missing, with errors and a price hidden at the end, is too much effort for a present.
interview.missing: I expected Meera to be included and the birthday memory to be the heart of the story. I also needed the final price before spending all that time creating the book, and a clear explanation of the photo privacy.
interview.trust: I was happy to enter the fictional family details, but I would not have trusted it with a child's photo without clear privacy information. The unexplained profile sync error and misleading gift-wrap selection also made me cautious.
interview.willingness_to_pay: Not for this version. Even a basic finished book would need to be around £25 including delivery to feel fair, and I would pay more only if the story really captured our memory, looked like the chosen style, and had no obvious errors.
interview.output_verdict: It was recognisably about Aarav, but it felt like an unproofed draft rather than a keepsake. I would be too disappointed and embarrassed to give it to him for his birthday.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the story around the supplied memory, with Aarav teaching Meera to find shapes in the clouds at Abbey Park on his fifth birthday.
recommendations.why: This is the personal part I wanted to buy. The current story leaves out Meera and turns the memory into something unrelated.

recommendations.change: Proofread the title and every page: fix “Adventrue”, “Aara”, possessives, pronouns, repeated text and the unfinished final sentence.
recommendations.why: The obvious mistakes make the present feel cheap and made me question whether the rest could be trusted.

recommendations.change: Match the generated artwork to the selected crayon style and keep Aarav, Meera and Rory visually consistent.
recommendations.why: The pictures are part of the gift. Getting pop-art instead of crayon, with generic characters, was disappointing.

recommendations.change: Use short, concrete sentences suitable for a five-year-old and remove frightening or unrelated events such as the threatening woods and storm.
recommendations.why: I need something gentle and readable for Aarav, not difficult vocabulary or a scary plot.

recommendations.change: Never pre-select premium gift wrap, and show the full price including delivery before I start creating the book.
recommendations.why: I need to know what it costs before spending ten minutes on a present. A £45.97 total with gift wrap already ticked felt like a trap.

recommendations.change: Explain what the paid regeneration button changes, how much it costs, and whether it is the only way to fix mistakes.
recommendations.why: I would not pay £4.99 without knowing what would improve, especially when the basic output was already wrong.

recommendations.change: Remove the unexplained profile sync error or explain plainly whether any details were affected.
recommendations.why: An error after a successful login immediately makes me wonder whether my account or family details are safe.

recommendations.change: Add clear privacy reassurance before the optional photo upload, including how the photo is used, stored and deleted.
recommendations.why: A child's photo is much more sensitive than basic story details, so I need to know what happens to it.

recommendations.change: Make the phone navigation fit properly and keep menu items on predictable lines.
recommendations.why: The wrapped navigation looks broken on my small phone and makes the site feel less trustworthy.

recommendations.change: Replace jargon with plain language and give a short explanation beside the reading-level choices.
recommendations.page: Home page and Reading level and illustration
recommendations.why: “Multimodal generative narrative engine” means nothing to me, and I had to guess what the reading-level labels meant.

recommendations.change: Make the next-page control a clearly labelled button and keep the gift-wrap checkbox attached to its label.
recommendations.page: Generated storybook preview and Hardcover checkout
recommendations.why: I use my phone one-handed, so unclear controls are easy to tap in the wrong place.

one_line_verdict: Quick to start and full of promise, but the unfinished, inaccurate story and sneaky checkout mean I would not give this to Aarav.
